Ukraine Received Only 24 US Patriots in 90 Days — President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine received only 24 Patriot interceptors from the United States over the past three months, despite facing intense Russian ballistic attacks and requiring roughly 350 interceptor missiles per month. Drones Hit Tolyatti Plant, Missiles Strike Oryol Defense Site — An overnight Ukrainian drone attack has struck the Tolyattikauchuk petrochemical plant in Russia’s Samara region, igniting a major blaze and forcing the evacuation of workers at the neighboring AvtoVAZ automotive factory. Concurrently, missiles struck the Proton defense microelectronics plant in Oryol, destroying a key workshop supplying components for T-90 and T-14 tanks, Pantsir-S1 systems, and Iskander-M and S-71 missiles.

Big Chill Between Turkey and Azerbaijan — Diplomatic relations between Turkey and Azerbaijan have deteriorated sharply following an address by Azerbaijan’s President Ilham Aliyev asserting sovereign independence, which Ankara has interpreted as a rebuke of Turkish influence. The dispute escalated with Baku imposing entry bans against 31 Turkish nationals, compounding earlier friction over Azerbaijan’s school headscarf ban. Turkish media expressed alarm over the total silence between Aliyev and T

Starlink, Starshield Speeds Exceed 161 km/h in Ukraine, MoD Says — Specialists from Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense and the Armed Forces confirmed on Saturday, Oct. 24, that Starlink and Starshield satellite terminals are now operating at velocities above 161 km/h (100 mph). Military communications teams continue tests at higher speeds to determine upper velocity limits and verify whether functionality has been unconditionally restored.

Rubio Says War Is About Donbas, Requires Diplomatic Compromise — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated during a press conference on Thursday, Oct. 22, that the war in Ukraine is fundamentally about the Donbas – representing roughly 11 percent of the country that Russia cannot seize militarily and Ukraine legitimately refuses to cede for sovereignty and security reasons. Emphasizing that the conflict cannot be resolved militarily, Rubio asserted that an end to hostilities requires diplomatic c

Oleshky: The Kremlin’s Next Propaganda Spectacle? — A potential ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky could open the way for a Kremlin-controlled press tour and gaslighting operation designed to shift blame for the humanitarian crisis onto Ukraine. Past operations in Mariupol, Kherson, Bucha and elsewhere show a recurring method: create or exploit suffering, deny responsibility, select compliant witnesses, and present propaganda as independent reporting.

Trump Weighs 200% Tariffs on Ukraine and Russia, Doubts Impact — US President Donald Trump claimed that tariffs had previously ended five wars and suggested applying 200 percent duties to Ukraine and Russia, though he conceded the move would not work because the US does not import enough from either country.

Zelensky Ready to Freeze Front Line to Halt War, Rejects Land Cession — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is prepared to freeze combat operations along existing front lines to bring an immediate halt to the war, while firmly rejecting territorial concessions and vowing never to recognize occupied lands as Russian sovereign territory. Clarifying that Russian forces currently control 19.3 percent of Ukraine rather than 25 percent, Zelensky stressed that halting the war along the

2 Injured as Russian Strike Hits House in Kyiv — A Russian aerial attack damaged a private residential home in Kyiv’s northern Obolonskyi district early Saturday, Oct. 24, injuring two civilians, the Kyiv City Military Administration reported. An air raid alert was declared around 3:42 a.m. as turbojet drones entered capital airspace. Nationwide, Ukrainian air defenses intercepted or suppressed 101 out of 126 Russian drones and cruise systems, including 50 turbojet Shaheds, with impacts recorded
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 23, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on October 23, 2026.

Carney Warns Starlink Manipulation Puts Ukrainian Lives at Risk — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned reported Starshield speed restrictions affecting Ukraine’s military operations, warning of direct casualties and serious national security risks. He cited Russia’s deadly attacks on Kyiv and raised concerns about dependence on privately controlled satellite networks.

Zelensky Lays Out Ukraine’s Conditions for Lasting Peace — Zelensky outlines Ukraine’s conditions for lasting peace, calling for a powerful army backed by at least 10 years of international funding, firm US and European security guarantees, and a ceasefire before broader negotiations. He also warns of delayed Patriot deliveries and persistent Starlink restrictions while proposing trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi.

‘Interceptors Still Not Coming’ – Zelensky Says US Has Yet to Authorize Patriot Deliveries — President Zelensky warned that previously agreed Patriot interceptor deliveries remain delayed, leaving Ukraine short of critical air defenses against Russian ballistic attacks. He also warned that Starlink and Starshield speed restrictions continue to hamper Ukrainian military operations despite reports that services had been restored.

Massive Blackout Hits Russian-Occupied Crimea After Drone Attacks — A massive blackout struck Russian-occupied Crimea overnight following reported drone attacks on energy infrastructure. Monitoring channels reported disabled substations and widespread outages, while Russian-installed officials confirmed disruptions in Sevastopol.

Melania Trump Announces Oleshky Truce as Ukraine and Russia Agree to Civilian Evacuations — US First Lady Melania Trump has announced a localized ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky to enable humanitarian deliveries and civilian evacuations. The initiative builds on her earlier efforts to reunite Ukrainian children separated from their families during Russia’s war.

Russia Pounds Kramatorsk With Aerial Bombs – 1 Killed, 6 Injured, Including 3 Children — A Russian airstrike on a residential neighborhood in Kramatorsk killed one civilian and wounded six others, including three children. Three FAB-250 aerial bombs damaged at least 27 residential buildings.

Ukraine’s Battlefield Lessons Reshape How Bundeswehr Trains Its Combat Medics — According to an official report on Monday, Oct. 19, Germany’s armed forces are overhauling how they train their combat medics, evacuate casualties and protect field hospitals. The move came after a Bundeswehr medical delegation studied battlefield care in Kyiv and Dnipro, where Ukrainian doctors reportedly told the team that drones now cause about 90% of combat wounds. According to the doctors, roughly 100,000 soldie

Zelensky Says Starlink Caps Persist as Kyiv Eyes November Talks With Russia, US — Speaking at the Hudson Institute on Friday, Oct. 23, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Starlink and Starshield restrictions remain in place, despite US President Donald Trump’s earlier claims that service was restored. Zelensky also said that agreed deliveries of interceptor missiles, used to deter Russian ballistic missiles, remain delayed. Trilateral meetings with Russia and the US are still expected to be held i

Russia’s Hot War on NATO: Airport Sabotage, Cruise Missiles & European Silence — Chuck Pfarrer exposes Russia’s escalating “hot war” against NATO and the technique European governments use to control public reaction: “Outrage Management.”

Oleshky Evacuation: Russia Announces Kherson Frontline ‘Silence Regime’ — Russia’s top general, Valery Gerasimov, announced a “silence regime” along the Kherson front starting Oct. 27 for a humanitarian operation in occupied Oleshky, two days earlier than the date set by the White House. The move follows Pope Leo XIV’s telephone calls to Russian President Vladimir Putin and President Volodymyr Zelensky to arrange safe evacuations and food deliveries to a city Ukraine’s senior authorities called

Air Defenses at Russian Drone Factory Linked to Forced Labor Rival Putin’s Residence — Russia has built 33 air-defense positions around its main Shahed drone production complex, placing it among the country’s most heavily protected sites. A separate report describes the exploitation of North Korean laborers, foreign women and Russian students working there.

1 Killed, 11 Injured as Russia Strikes Dnipropetrovsk Region Nearly 70 Times — Russian forces struck four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 70 times on Friday, Oct. 23, killing one person and wounding 11. According to the head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Hanzha, Dnipro faced the brunt of the attack, with a private house destroyed and a body recovered from the rubble.

Ukraine Ends Blanket Deferments, Ties Full Exemptions to Military Service — Ukraine’s government, led by Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, has finalized an overhaul of its worker deferment system, effectively ending unconditional 100% deferments for defense and energy companies. The changes target firms created solely to shield workers from the draft, while companies could still defer all staff if they regularly send some of their employees to serve in the military.

White House Says Russia, Ukraine Agree to Oleshky Truce — The White House said Friday, Oct. 23, that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to a local ceasefire in occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine’s Kherson region, beginning Oct. 29. The announcement credited US First Lady Melania Trump with mediating the agreement, which is intended to allow humanitarian aid into the city and prepare civilian evacuations. Kyiv and Moscow had not immediately commented.

Romania Blames Russia for Drone Strike That Sank Black Sea Ship — Romanian President Nicușor Dan blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank the Comoros-flagged Khoryv near Constanța on Oct. 23. The sinking follows a series of attacks on commercial shipping as NATO prepares to reinforce surveillance in the Black Sea.

All 4 Moscow Airports Halt Flights as Sheremetyevo Issues Air Raid Alert — Russia suspended arrivals and departures at Moscow’s four airports on Oct. 23. Sheremetyevo issued an air raid alert, while Vnukovo warned passengers of prolonged waits, including aboard aircraft.

‘We Are Christians, Good People’: Russian Media Tycoon Urges Nuclear Strike on Ukraine — Appearing on Piers Morgan’s show, Konstantin Malofeyev criticized Putin for not using nuclear weapons and proposed targeting Western arms depots in Ukraine. The media tycoon previously advocated a tactical nuclear attack followed by public executions.

Belarus Still Hosts Russian Drone Relays, Ukraine’s Border Service Says — Andriy Demchenko, spokesman for Ukraine’s State Border Guard Service (DPSU), said in a televised interview on Friday that Belarus continues to host relay stations used by Russian drones. He said border guards have not recorded Russian or Belarusian units moving toward the Ukrainian border. Ukraine said in June that the relays had stopped working, but Demchenko said in September that they were active again.

Abu Dhabi Considered for Ukraine-Russia-US Talks in November — Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Abu Dhabi is being considered for renewed talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States. Moscow has proposed discussing postwar security, while Kyiv is seeking an early meeting and enforceable guarantees against another Russian attack.

443 Drones Downed: Russian Airfield, Chemical Plant and Tax Data Center Targeted in Overnight Attacks — Drone attacks reportedly damaged infrastructure near Voronezh’s Baltimor airfield, a chemical plant in Perm Krai and a Russian tax service data center in Nizhny Novgorod region. Russian officials reported three injuries and said 443 drones had been downed nationwide.

Ukraine Returns 270 in New POW Exchange — Ukraine has brought home 270 people in a prisoner exchange with Russia, including military personnel and nine civilians. Five of those released were previously believed to have died in the July 2022 attack on the Olenivka prison, Zelensky said.

Witkoff Meets Putin: the Upshot? — European and international media criticize Donald Trump’s Ukraine mediation efforts, warning that his envoy Steve Witkoff’s praise of Vladimir Putin undermines diplomatic credibility. Commentators argue that Moscow is exploiting US eagerness for a peace deal to buy time, weaken Ukraine and divide Western allies. They stress that Ukraine will resist surrender, while doubts grow over Trump’s motives, security guarantees and prospects for lasting peace.

Russian Diesel Tanker Heads to New York After Trump-Putin Deal — A shipment of around 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel set sail for the US on Thursday, following a Trump-Putin agreement to resume Russian diesel exports. Its expected Nov. 7 arrival comes after the Nov. 3 elections, and the amount is estimated to last the US just shy of two hours of use.

Ukraine Still Recording Starshield Connectivity Losses at 161 Kph, Defense Ministry Source Says — Ukraine’s defense ministry says satellite connectivity losses at speeds of 161 kph are still in place, despite US President Donald Trump’s claim that SpaceX owner Elon Musk restored the service. SpaceX and the White House have blamed one another for the restrictions, which followed the US diesel deal with Russia, as Washington pressured Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian refineries without securing a b

US Reportedly Plans to ‘Offer’ Ukraine EU Membership for Dropping NATO Bid — A US peace proposal reportedly ‘offers’ Ukraine EU membership and investment in exchange for abandoning its NATO bid. The package also envisages economic incentives for Russia. No agreement has been announced, and EU accession would require approval from the bloc’s members.

One Dead, Three Missing From Ship in ‘Distress’ in Black Sea — Romania launched a rescue operation after a cargo ship carrying 13 Ukrainian and Azerbaijani crew members sent a distress signal in the Black Sea. Nine people were rescued and one body recovered, with three crew still missing, amid a series of suspected Russian drone attacks on shipping in the region.

US Reportedly Proposes Nord Stream Revival in Ukraine Peace Talks — US proposals reportedly include reviving Nord Stream, easing sanctions and expanding business ties with Russia. Ukrainian negotiators fear economic concessions could precede an end to the war, while access to Europe’s gas market remains outside Washington’s control.

Zelensky Yacht Fake: How Russia’s Doppelgänger Network Works — Russia’s Doppelgänger network tracked how fabricated stories about Ukraine reached Western audiences, according to an investigation by The Insider. Internal files included JD Vance’s remarks about a Ukrainian minister buying a yacht, alongside reports on other disinformation campaigns.

Russia to Unveil ‘Anti-Drone Dome’ at Africa Summit — Russia will pitch its planned “Anti-Drone Dome” air defense system to African partners at next week’s Moscow summit, even as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to hit Russian oil refineries and other critical infrastructure, exposing gaps in Moscow’s air defenses.

Austria Expels Four Russian Diplomats: Foreign Ministry — Austria has ordered four Russian diplomats to leave the country over activities deemed incompatible with their diplomatic status. The expulsions come amid heightened European concerns about Russian espionage following Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Denmark Delivers Over 50,000 Cannon Rounds for Ukraine’s F-16s — Ukraine’s Defense Ministry says Denmark delivered more than 50,000 rounds of 20 mm ammunition for its F-16 fighters. The ammunition is already being used in air-defense operations after Copenhagen redirected part of a planned sale with another country’s agreement.

Russia Pounds Kyiv’s Energy Infrastructure: How Are Residents Preparing for Winter? — As Russian attacks threaten Kyiv’s energy infrastructure ahead of winter, residents share their thoughts about power cuts, heating shortages and the city’s preparedness. While some are preparing to leave, most say they intend to stay but question whether the authorities are doing enough to protect the capital.

5 European Leaders Floated as Potential Negotiators With Putin — Five European leaders, including Italy’s Giorgia Meloni and Finland’s Alexander Stubb, are being considered to represent Europe in potential talks with Vladimir Putin as European capitals seek a greater role in efforts to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Oleksandr Levchenko: Financing Ukraine’s Recovery Must Combine Capital, Risk Management, and Responsible AI — Oleksandr Levchenko explains how risk-adjusted finance, digital resilience, and carefully governed AI can help attract investment and strengthen Ukraine’s postwar recovery. He also discusses the opportunities and limits of artificial intelligence in the financial sector.

Russia Strikes Odesa Energy Facility, Claims Naval Drone Sites Hit as Attacks Injure 2 Elsewhere — Russian attacks damaged energy and civilian infrastructure in southern Ukraine’s Odesa region overnight, while strikes on central Ukraine’s Poltava and Dnipropetrovsk regions damaged railway facilities, homes and other infrastructure. Two people were injured in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukrainian officials said.

A Prisoner Release From Hell: the Potentially Catastrophic Human Cost of Trump’s Deal — The release of Stephen Hubbard is now being used by Trump as a diplomatic trophy to justify the isolation and abandonment of Ukraine for an American realignment with Putin’s Russia.

Poland Probes Plot to Torch Drone Factory Supplying Ukraine — Polish prosecutors are investigating an alleged plot to set fire to Flytronic, a factory producing reconnaissance drones used by Ukraine, after a Russia-linked recruiter reportedly offered $30,000 for the attack. The case has been referred to Poland’s Internal Security Agency.

Drones Hit Occupied Luhansk, Disrupting Communications as Russia Strikes Ukrainian Power Plant — Drones struck communications infrastructure in Russian-occupied Luhansk early Oct. 23, disrupting services, while a Russian attack forced a DTEK thermal power plant to halt generation. Ukraine’s air defenses reported neutralizing 140 of 176 Russian drones launched since Thursday evening.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 22, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on October 22, 2026.

‘Not Another Budapest Memorandum’ – Kyiv Seeks US Security Guarantees Backed by Congress — President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine is negotiating Article 5-style security guarantees with Washington that would require US congressional approval. Rejecting a repeat of the failed Budapest Memorandum, he calls for a comprehensive defense framework combining American commitments, NATO membership, European support and a strong Ukrainian military.

‘Putin Is Using Hitler’s Tactics’ – Ranking US Senator Slams Russian Attacks on Ukrainian Cities — Senator Jeanne Shaheen compares Russia’s bombardment of Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure to Hitler’s attacks on Britain, warning that Putin seeks to break civilian morale. She joins bipartisan criticism of US envoy Steve Witkoff for calling Putin a “humanitarian,” with Republican lawmakers responding, “WTF, Steve?”

Russia Launches Massive Drone Attack on Sumy as Moscow Continues Strikes Despite Peace Talks — Russian forces launched a massive drone attack on Sumy early Friday, Oct. 23, injuring at least two civilians and damaging residential areas. The assault followed deadly strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions as Moscow signaled readiness for renewed peace negotiations while continuing its bombardment.

‘Starshield Still Limited’ – Zelensky Says Restrictions Continue to Hamper Ukraine’s Drone Defenses — President Volodymyr Zelensky tells CNN that Ukraine’s Starshield military communications remain restricted despite reports of restored service, limiting its ability to intercept Russian drones. He confirms US missile-warning intelligence has resumed, urges more Patriot interceptors and opposes easing sanctions on Moscow.

Trump Says Musk Restored Ukraine’s Starshield — President Donald Trump says Elon Musk restored Ukraine’s military-grade Starshield satellite service after speed restrictions disrupted Ukrainian strike and interceptor drones. The US president declined to confirm reports that he personally intervened.

‘Putin Has Killed Thousands’ – Downing Street Rebukes Witkoff for Calling Russian Leader ‘Humanitarian’ — Downing Street rejects US envoy Steve Witkoff’s description of Vladimir Putin as a “humanitarian,” citing thousands killed in Russia’s war and systematic attacks on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure.

‘More Money Means More Dead Ukrainians’ – Kasparov Warns Against Deals With Moscow — Garry Kasparov warns that exchanging Russian political prisoners for sanctions relief would allow Moscow to build more missiles and drones, while sharply criticizing the prospect of striking deals with Putin.

Russia Strikes Crowded Market in Lozova, Killing 2, Wounding 36 — Russian forces struck a crowded market in Lozova, Kharkiv region on Thursday, Oct. 22, killing two women and injuring another 36 people. Two of those wounded were treated for acute stress reactions. According to regional authorities, the attack was carried out with a jet-powered Shahed drone and a Banderol missile during the middle of the day, damaging market pavilions, private houses, apartment buildings, private vehicles and a c

Ukraine Expands Satellite Cooperation With Finland as Starlink Doubts Linger — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Thursday, Oct. 22 that he signed seven agreements with Finland’s Prime Minister Petteri Orpo, including deals to expand Kyiv’s use of Finnish satellite capabilities through Nokia and ICEYE. The total value of the agreements amount to over €300 million (roughly $337 million), as Ukraine and Europe weigh alternatives to Starlink that disrupted Ukrainian drone operations without

‘Wrong and Unacceptable’: Zelensky Accuses Trump of Shifting Iran Blame to Kyiv — President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Donald Trump of unfairly blaming him for Russia’s aggression and using Ukraine to divert attention from problems surrounding Iran. In an interview with Steven Bartlett, he rejected claims linking Ukrainian refinery strikes to rising US diesel prices. Zelensky said Washington should press Putin for an energy ceasefire and supply Ukraine with air defense missiles.

Vance: Starlink Use Depends on US Policy Toward Kyiv, Moscow – Not Musk — Speaking to reporters before departing for a rally in North Platte, Nebraska on Thursday, Oct. 22, US Vice President JD Vance said that the dispute over Ukraine’s Starlink restrictions should not fall on SpaceX CEO Elon Musk himself, framing the issue as a matter of US policy on the war. He called Europe’s reliance on the company ironic, while also noting that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to negotiate after senior US env

Russian Shahed Drone Strikes Private Home in Zhytomyr, Injuring 8, Including 2 Children — Russian forces struck a private house in the Zhytomyr community on Thursday, Oct. 22, with a jet-powered Shahed drone, leaving eight people wounded – including two children. The attack struck a region located in western Ukraine, far from the front line, after drone strikes damaged energy infrastructure and eight homes the previous day.

Sloviansk Expands Forced Evacuation Zone for Families With Children to Entire Community — Regional authorities have extended mandatory evacuation of families with children to the entire Sloviansk community after Russian forces struck the settlements of the Donetsk region 42 times on Wednesday, injuring two boys aged seven and 12. According to Donetsk regional governor Vadym Filashkin on Thursday, 215 people, including 68 children, had already been evacuated from the front line.

Russia Hits Central Kyiv With Cluster Missile — Russia attacked Kyiv’s historic center with an Iskander ballistic missile carrying a K5 cluster warhead, presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said. He described a weapon designed to disperse 58 explosive elements over a wide area and accused Moscow of targeting civilians. The statement followed an overnight barrage that killed one person and injured at least 24 across the capital.

Germany Arrests Ukrainian Suspected of Spying for Russia — Germany said it has arrested a Ukrainian man identified as Vadym Y. suspected of spying for Russia, whose tasks included collecting intelligence on weaponry and NATO’s eastern flank defense. Europe has warned of an uptick in hybrid attacks from Russia, with Berlin documenting over 165 suspected sabotage cases in the first eight months of 2026 alone.

‘Abandon Ukraine, Embrace Putin’: Bill Clinton Slams Trump as Hillary Calls Him a ‘Willing Putin Puppet’ — Hillary Clinton called Trump a “willing Putin puppet,” alleging that he prioritizes the Russian leader over US security. Bill Clinton separately accused Trump of abandoning Ukraine and treating US allies “like dirt.”

Trump Could Force Putin to Negotiate but Hasn’t, Zelensky Says — Zelensky said Trump has the leverage to bring Putin to negotiations but has not used it. He warned that surrendering Sloviansk and Kramatorsk could expose more Ukrainian territory to Russian advances and undermine security guarantees.

Zelensky Did Not Expect Russia to Launch Full-Scale Invasion — Zelensky recalled telling his family that Russia’s invasion had begun and described visiting liberated Bucha as his hardest day of the war.

Witkoff Meets Putin: Any Progress on Ukraine? — Western media doubt the prospects for peace in Ukraine following Putin’s meeting with Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff in Saint Petersburg. Commentators argue that Moscow shows little willingness to compromise, while Trump’s policies may embolden Russia and weaken Western unity. Critics suggest Putin is exploiting US political pressures to gain strategic advantages, raising concerns about Ukraine’s future, security guarantees, and the credibility of Tru

Russia’s New Filin Missile Uses US, Chinese Electronics — Russia began using the Filin cruise missile against Ukraine in late summer, HUR said. Its analysis identified 35 US and 22 Chinese electronic components, alongside a Russian engine and navigation equipment shared with other Russian weapons.

Ukraine Reports Record Russian War Losses in a Day — Ukraine said it has set a record for Russian troops killed or wounded on Oct. 21, 2026, with the country’s General Staff claiming 2,250 Russian casualties within 24 hours, topping the previous record of 2,200 set in December 2024. Ukrainian sources attribute losses to Russia’s open infantry tactics across open ground being picked off by drones. The record also counters Trump’s claim that Ukraine is failing to stop Russian attacks.

NATO to Open Centralized Arms Purchases for Ukraine — Under a new partnership with the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA), Ukraine will be allowed to place orders for weapons, ammunition and military supplies via the alliance’s centralized procurement channels. The decision comes as the alliance’s PURL program comes under threat during the latest row between Kyiv and Washington, though it’s unclear if the new channel can provide the air defense Kyiv urgently needs as winter approaches.

Ukraine Receives 252 Bodies From Russia, Identification to Follow — Ukraine has received 252 bodies in a new repatriation operation, according to the country’s Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War. Russia says the remains belong to Ukrainian military personnel, but their identities must still be established through forensic examinations. The operation involved Ukrainian security and defense agencies, with assistance from the International Committee of the Red Cross.

Report: Shahed Factory Gets Putin-Style Air Defenses — Russia has expanded air defenses around its Alabuga drone production hub in Tatarstan, where journalists identified 33 defensive positions. The concentration is comparable in number to defenses around Vladimir Putin’s Valdai residence, according to Radio Liberty. New satellite imagery shows additional towers and platforms around the complex as Russia continues expanding production of drones used against Ukraine.

Putin the Humanist? 10 Ways Russia Has Shown Its ‘Humanity’ in Ukraine — US envoy Steve Witkoff called Vladimir Putin a “humanist.” The record of Russia’s war against Ukraine includes the killings in Bucha, the bombing of Mariupol’s theater and maternity hospital, the transfer of Ukrainian children to Russia, torture of prisoners of war – and a baby killed in a stroller in a Russian drone strike.

‘Humanitarian’: Trump Weighs In on Putin Praise Amid Backlash — Donald Trump offered a qualified response when asked whether he agreed with envoy Steve Witkoff’s description of Vladimir Putin as a “humanitarian.” He suggested the term could apply to the release of American detainee Stephen Hubbard but declined to give a broader assessment. Republican lawmakers condemned Witkoff’s praise, while criticism of the administration’s wider Russia policy continued.

Europe Weighs Naming Envoy to Negotiate With Putin on Ukraine — European leaders are weighing who should negotiate with Vladimir Putin as fears grow that the US could sideline Europe in a Ukraine peace deal. The Kremlin’s suggestion of former German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder has sparked backlash, exposing divisions over who should represent Europe in potential talks.

Finland to Invest in Anti-Personnel Mines After Ottawa Convention Withdrawal — Finland formally withdrew from the Ottawa Convention, the anti-personnel landmine (APL) ban, in January because of the perceived growing threat from Moscow. Finnish media reports that Helsinki is preparing to build up a new stockpile of APLs with which to protect its border with Russia.

An Investor’s Stress Test: How NHSU Rules Are Driving European Companies Away — Ukraine’s healthcare reimbursement rules are raising concerns among European investors, as private laboratory provider Synevo reports that nearly 700,000 tests were not recognized. Unequal treatment of private and state-run providers threatens fair competition, undermines investor confidence, and risks complicating Ukraine’s EU integration efforts.

‘We Outplayed Them’: Ukraine Claims First Underground Counteroffensive — Ukraine’s Khartiia Corps says Operation Veles sent troops through underground infrastructure to strike behind Russian lines and disrupt a threat to Kupiansk. The corps reported more than 30 Russian prisoners captured and described the maneuver as the world’s first full-scale underground counteroffensive.

Zelensky on Overnight Strike: ‘Russian ‘Humanists’ Launch 21 Ballistic Missiles at Kyiv in 3 Waves’ — Russia launched 21 ballistic missile strikes in three waves against Kyiv following the latest negotiations, Zelensky said. He called for stronger air defenses, faster missile deliveries and tougher sanctions, arguing that Russia must face real pressure to end the killing.

Buyer and Supplier: How China Sustains Russia’s War — China’s part in sustaining Russia’s wartime economy goes well beyond that of a major trading partner. In energy, Chinese demand gives Russia a critical outlet for crude oil and other fossil fuels. But given the geopolitical context, India will be punished more by sanctions.

‘Red Line Crossed’: Germany Raises Russian Sabotage Threat to ‘Significant’ for First Time — Germany’s armed forces have raised the Russian sabotage threat to “significant,” the military’s second-highest internal alert level, after an explosives-carrying drone was found near Wunstorf air base. Berlin is strengthening site-specific security measures amid concerns over Russian hybrid warfare.

Russian Attacks Kill 4 Civilians, Injure at Least a Dozen Across Ukraine in Overnight Drone Strike — Russian attacks killed 4 civilians and injured at least 14 others in Donetsk, Kharkiv, Chernihiv regions, including two boys aged 10 and 13. Drone strikes also damaged civilian vehicles and buildings in Kharkiv and Sumy, while a warehouse fire broke out in Kirovohrad region.

630 Drones Toward Moscow, Russian Military Repair Plant Reportedly Hit — Moscow Mayor claimed 630 drones had been heading toward Moscow since Oct. 21, while footage analyzed by Astra suggests a strike hit the 75th Arsenal military repair plant in Serpukhov. Russian officials also reported drone attacks and damage across several other regions.

Kremlin Confirms Lukoil Negotiations With Washington — The Kremlin confirmed talks with Washington over sanctioned Russian oil giant Lukoil’s $22 billion foreign assets, as the US Treasury extended authorization for sale negotiations until Nov. 21.

Witkoff Reveals US Treasury Working With Putin’s Envoy on Economic Ties — Witkoff confirmed direct US Treasury talks with Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev on economic cooperation alongside Ukraine peace negotiations. Putin outlined Russian diesel shipments to the US and offered fertilizer exports.

‘Capitulating to a Dictator Shows Weakness’ – Republican Senator Slams Trump’s Russia Policy — Republican Senator John Curtis criticized President Donald Trump’s Russia policy, warning that sanctions relief, Russian energy purchases and restrictions affecting Ukraine’s military capabilities are emboldening Vladimir Putin. Drawing on his recent visit to Ukraine, Curtis called for stronger American leadership and continued support for Kyiv.

Trump Envoy Grilled for Calling Putin a ‘Humanitarian’ — US special envoy Steve Witkoff sparked criticism from Republican lawmakers after calling Vladimir Putin a “humanitarian” during talks in St. Petersburg. Senator Thom Tillis sharply rebuked the envoy, while President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance defended his remarks following the release of an American detainee.

Russia Pounds Kyiv in Overnight Missile and Drone Barrage – 1 Dead, 24 Injured, Including 4 Children — Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks on Kyiv killed one person and injured 24 others, including 4 children. Strikes damaged metro infrastructure on the South Bridge, an ambulance station, six emergency vehicles, homes and businesses.
